A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 18-page documents, including Appendices A–B. Text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that the scientific text, equations, figures, and tables match.

before.justification: v2 reports original DFT and DFT2 experiments in Section 7 and Appendix B, including benchmark performance, baseline comparisons, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and all appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 and Algorithms 1–2 retain identical DFT and DFT2 objectives, scoring functions, negative sampling, moving-average updates, and optimization procedures.

E1.justification: The MetaMathQA, UltraFeedback, and UltraChat training coverage and all mathematical reasoning, general-language, and instruction-following evaluations are unchanged, including appendix test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SFT, SPIN, SimPO, SimPO-SFT, KTO, ORPO, and DPO-p. Comparator membership also matches within every other main-text and appendix comparison.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A retain identical model configurations, training budgets, sampling settings, and evaluation procedures, including the benchmark shots, metrics, and chat-template settings in Table 7.

E4.justification: Section 7.2 and Appendix B retain the same training-dynamics analyses and experiments on moving-average coefficients, negative-sample counts, base models, prompting strategies, and sampling temperatures.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 1 reports DFT accuracy of 79.15 on GSM8K and 28.34 on MATH in both versions.

T1.justification: The discriminative-likelihood definitions, importance-sampling reformulation, gradient and numerical-stability derivations, and DFT2 approximation in Sections 3–6 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about discriminative finetuning without reward models or human preference data, efficient optimization, and competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications match, including the discussion of AlpacaEval2 performance and output length, and the suspected overfitting explanation for increasing the negative-sample count to four.

D1.justification: Implementation frameworks, hyperparameters, hardware, training and generation times, sampling instructions, and code-access information are unchanged, including the details in Appendix A and Section B.5.

R1.justification: Section 2, the comparisons with prior approaches, and the reference list are unchanged. The first-page conference designation edit does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 changes Tuo Zhao’s affiliation marker from 2 to 3, the conference ordinal from 41st to 42nd, and the arXiv version/date stamp. Page 10 changes “Impact Statements” to “Impact Statement.” The narrative and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–12 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The small textual edits do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: v3 makes only limited affiliation, publication-label, and heading edits. The scientific reasoning, experimental evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information—including both appendices—are identical, establishing no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
